title: Mohanlal Is Teaming Up With Dileesh Pothan — and Malayalam Cinema's Best Pairing Hasn't Even Started Yet
excerpt: The superstar and the 'Maheshinte Prathikaram' director are finally joining forces. Asif Ali rounds out a cast that has Kerala's NRI audience counting down from Dubai to Dallas.
body:
It's one of those announcements that makes you wonder why it didn't happen sooner. Mohanlal and Dileesh Pothan — arguably Malayalam cinema's biggest star and its most acclaimed working director — are officially collaborating on a new film.

Producer Antony Perumbavoor confirmed the project, which will be produced by Shibu Baby John. Asif Ali, fresh off a career-best run of films, is reportedly cast in a key supporting role. The film will be directed by Dileesh Pothan, whose track record — *Maheshinte Prathikaram*, *Thondimuthalum Driksakshiyum*, *Joji* — reads like a masterclass in humanist Malayalam filmmaking.

## Why This Pairing Matters

Dileesh Pothan has built his reputation on films that are quiet, textured, and devastating in their emotional precision. Mohanlal, at 65, has spent the last few years oscillating between franchise spectacles (*Drishyam 3* releases May 21, *L2: Empuraan* was a blockbuster earlier this year) and smaller, more personal projects.

The combination is electric because it's unexpected. Pothan doesn't make star vehicles. His films are ensemble-driven, character-first stories where the biggest name in the cast often plays the most understated role. If he's casting Mohanlal, it's not for a mass-hero entry scene — it's because he has a character that demands Mohanlal the actor, not Mohanlal the brand.

That distinction matters. Pothan extracted what many consider Fahadh Faasil's finest performance in *Joji* (streaming on Amazon Prime internationally) and turned Asif Ali from a reliable romantic lead into a serious dramatic force. What he might draw out of Mohanlal is the question keeping Malayalam film Twitter up at night.

## The Asif Ali Factor

Asif Ali's inclusion is a signal. The actor has been on a remarkable upswing, delivering critically acclaimed performances that have expanded his range far beyond the romcom territory he once occupied. In a Dileesh Pothan film opposite Mohanlal, he'll likely play the grounding presence — the everyman against the superstar's gravity.

For NRI audiences who've followed Asif's evolution on streaming platforms (most of his recent work is available on Disney+ Hotstar and SonyLIV internationally), this is a reunion of sorts: Pothan directed Asif to a career-defining performance in *Maheshinte Prathikaram*, the 2016 sleeper hit that put both of them on the map.

## Where *Drishyam 3* Fits

The timing is deliberate. Mohanlal's *Drishyam 3* hits theatres on May 21, four days from now, and he's already teasing *Drishyam 4* and *5* — a franchise play that could run for years. The Pothan collaboration sits at the opposite end of his creative spectrum: an auteur-driven film that could remind audiences of the actor behind the franchise.

For the Kerala diaspora — and there's a massive NRI Malayali population across the Gulf, the US, UK, and Canada — this announcement lands differently. These are audiences who grew up watching Mohanlal in Priyadarshan comedies and Mani Ratnam dramas. A Dileesh Pothan collaboration doesn't just promise a good film. It promises a *specific kind* of good film: one that trusts its audience, rewards patience, and doesn't need a single fight sequence to hold attention.

## What We Know (and Don't)

Details beyond the core team are scarce. No title has been announced. No plot details have leaked. The script's authorship — Pothan typically works with writer Syam Pushkaran, his creative partner across all four of his films — hasn't been confirmed, though it would be a surprise if Pushkaran weren't involved.

Production timelines suggest shooting could begin after Mohanlal wraps his current commitments, likely in late 2026. For now, this is a promise: two of Malayalam cinema's most interesting minds, finally in the same room.

*Mohanlal's Drishyam 3 releases in theatres worldwide on May 21, 2026.*
